page: Microsoft Azure M64bds_1_v3 is a memory-optimized server instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8473C processor running at 4.0 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it features 64 dedicated vCPUs (32 physical cores with hyper-threading) and a substantial 105 MB L3 cache. The server is equipped with 1397.0 GB of RAM, providing approximately 21.83 GB of memory per core. It includes 3072 GB of local SSD storage and supports Premium Storage, but does not feature any GPUs.

In benchmark testing, the instance demonstrates strong memory performance, with read-only large block memory bandwidth reaching 216.95 GB/sec and write bandwidth at 92.66 GB/sec. CPU performance is robust, highlighted by a Passmark CPU score of 66425.61 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 19691.0. The processor's advanced instruction sets, including AVX-512 and AMX, contribute to strong performance in extended instructions and cryptography. For database operations, the server achieved a Passmark database score of 28843.47 and processed 70.71 million Redis SET operations per second. However, for large-scale LLM text generation using a 70B model, performance is weak at 2.58 tokens/sec due to the lack of hardware GPU acceleration.

Given its high memory-to-vCPU ratio and dedicated compute resources, this instance offers high resource density for memory-bound workloads. The inclusion of 3072 GB of local SSD storage provides a cost-efficient alternative to relying solely on external block storage for high-throughput data access. This server is configured for large-scale databases, in-memory caching systems like Redis, data analytics, and memory-intensive enterprise applications.
